messages.subject: how to separate more than two peaks in a chromosome?
messages.subject_clean: how to separate more than two peaks in a chromosome?
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I'm following the r/qtl book to analyse my QTLs. I got 3 peaks respectively in 3 chromosomes, as shown in the attached picture 1, one of which on chromosome 8 is with huge confidence interval. So I think there may be more than one genes in that peak and I want to use methods for multiple QTLs to separate them.

I first ran scaneone, and got the results as shown in attached picture 2. Then I controlled the QTL on chr8 by running makeqtl and addqtl of position 8@118, and the result showed me that there may be another peak at 8@24 (as shown in attached picture 3). So I expected that if I control the QTLS on chr2 and chr3, then I will find two peaks seperately at 8@120 and 8@24 on chr8.

But the problem came. After I ran add pair command, the result gave me two peaks at 8@75 and 8@100 with very weak evidence (shown in attached picture 4). So I don't understand why the result is so different from what I expected according to the results from previous steps.

Btw, when I plot the addpair result, I got the graph as shown in attached picture 5, indicating three locations interacting in chr8. But the evidence is very weak.

Could somebody explain a bit for me? Are there more than one gene in the peak on chr8? If so, did I do the right thing to separate them? Thanks in advance!

Here is my code:
out1.bin <- scanone(AllChrSuperNew1, pheno.col=2, method=c("em"))
summary(out1.bin)
qtl8 <- makeqtl(AllChrSuperNew1,chr = 8, pos =118.8633 ,what="prob")
summary(fitqtl(AllChrSuperNew1,pheno.col=2,method = "hk",qtl=qtl8,get.ests = TRUE))
out1.c8 <- addqtl(AllChrSuperNew1,pheno.col=2,qtl=qtl8)
summary(out1.c8)
plot(out1.c8,ylab="LOD Score")
qtl23 <- makeqtl(AllChrSuperNew1,chr= c(2,3),pos=c(136.8572,151.0700),what="prob")
out1.ap <- addpair(AllChrSuperNew1,qtl=qtl23,chr=8,method = "hk",verbose=FALSE)
summary(out1.ap)

It looks like you’re approaching this correctly. In my view, the 3 peaks you see in the initial LOD curve on chr 8 are not strong indications for multiple QTL on the chromosome. The multiple-QTL analyses you’ve done, which provide only weak evidence for additional QTL, suggest to me that those initial bumps where just bumps and not additional QTL.

Karl

I was told that I need QTL results in bp or Mbp for publication. What is the best way to get that?

Thanks

For calculation of genotype probabilities, the marker positions need to be in cM. With very dense markers it probably doesn't much matter, but basepairs is generally not what you want, and if you say step=1 in calc.genoprob when you have a map in basepairs, you're asking for all calculations to be performed every basepair, and that why you'll have memory issues. If you use step=0 it does calculations just at the markers.

I would at least convert to Mbp rather than bp. And then for the mouse genome, you could divide by 2 to get a rough estimate of cM. Better would be to use a mouse genetic map, for which the "mouse map converter" tool is useful: http://cgd.jax.org/mousemapconverter

If you need to get positions back to Mbp, you could either focus solely on the marker positions, whose Mbp positions you already know, or you can use interpPositions() to interpolate between the genetic and physical maps, and replacemap() to replace genetic map positions with physical positions.

karl

I've read in the discussion group about getting positions into cM. If left in bp memory problems can occur for calc.genoprob with a step equal to 1. Rqtl tries to insert psuedomarkers between every bp. I did have this problem. Is it ok to set the step equal to 0? I've done that and get results. I was told that I need QTL results in bp or Mbp for publication. What is the best way to get that?
>

When I used qtlpvl package to perform the qtl1v2 analysis (simulation=1000, method=fast), i got the result that p value is not significant and all these phenotypes have the same one QTL.

So now I wonder in my result should I say all these phenotypes share the same QTL (as the multiple trait QTL mapping suggested) or should I say there are different genes involved (as the interval mapping results suggested) in these phenotypes?

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl et al.
I am working with a selfed F1 population of a highly polyploid outbred plant. The parents of the F1 are unknown and the markers are all simplex: dominant, phase unknown and segregate in a 3:1 ratio.
My goal is to impute genotyping errors and missing data from a map generated in joinmap4.

How would you suggest treating this type of population in R/qtl. My instinct is to use crosstype = "f2", where markers are either 'BB' or 'not BB'. However, if I treat it as an F2, when I fill will imputations, the dominant alleles get partitioned into AA and AB. How can the imputations know which it is, given that there is no information in the genotype matrix to distinguish between AA and AB. When I fill will argmax, all dominant alleles are assigned to AB. This isn't right either and leads to incorrect map estimations.

Any advice is much appreciated.
Thanks,
John

Here is an example of the issue I am running into.

```
map = seq(1,100,1)
names(map) <- paste0("a",map)

# simulate a cross with only dominant markers
cross = sim.cross(map = list(chr1 = map),
          n.ind = 100, type = "f2",
          partial.missing.prob = 1,
          error.prob = .05, missing.prob = .01,
          map.function = "kosambi")

# keep only markers with BB/non-BB genotypes
gt = geno.table(cross)
todrop = rownames(gt)[gt$AA>0]
cross = drop.markers(cross, markers = todrop)
summary(cross)

fill.imp = fill.geno(cross, method = "imp", map.function = "kosambi",
                     error.prob = .05)
fill.am <http://fill.am> = fill.geno(cross, method = "argmax", map.function = "kosambi",
                     error.prob = .05)

summary(fill.imp)
summary(fill.am <http://fill.am>)
```
